_note: The closed gate vocabulary: the named MOMENTS a practice can fire at.
GATES are the fourth loading channel: a moment, not a place. A practice whose
occasion is a moment cannot be reached by a glob, however well written.
tools/precedent_gate.py loads a gate's practices at the moment it is reached.
Until 2026-09-29 this file also listed every on-demand practice with the
reason for its applies_to, and a harness test failed when a practice had no
entry. That second list was the cause of the failure it tested for: adding
or deleting a practice meant remembering to edit this file too, and the list
had already drifted on gates nobody checked. The reason now lives in each
practice's own frontmatter, as applies_to_why (and gates_why), so a practice
cannot arrive or leave without it (practice: upstream-fix; Morgan,
2026-09-29: prevent the cause, don't only check for it later).
precedent_check.py's routing-reason check refuses an on-demand practice with
no applies_to_why.
THE RULE the routing pass settled on, kept here because it governs every
applies_to_why: a glob is justified only where the path identifies the
practice's DISTINGUISHING condition, not merely a necessary one. 'A rule is
being written' is necessary for volatile-rules-carry-dates and not
distinguishing; 'a new rule is being written' IS distinguishing for
cite-the-incident. '**' means the path channel never fires for that
practice: it is reached through the occasion index, a gate, or a check, and
its applies_to_why says which.
The gate vocabulary is closed: tools/verify_harness.py refuses an unknown gate name, and refuses a gate with no practices. Each gate names a moment with a real invocation point in this repo.
gates.review: reviewing work, or a review finding a defect
gates.reply: ending a turn and writing the reply — the stop hook
